page_title: Why you should pick strong consistency, whenever possible

sources.entry: Why you should pick strong consistency, whenever possible

summary.name: Cloud Spanner (strong consistency essay)
summary.one_liner: A 2018 Google Cloud blog essay by Mike Curtiss arguing for strong consistency in databases, using Cloud Spanner's external consistency as the example.
use_cases: Choosing between strong and eventual consistency
Designing financial balance or ledger updates
summary.what_it_does: The page is an essay explaining consistency models (consistency, serializability, linearizability, strong and eventual consistency) and how Cloud Spanner provides external consistency across rows, regions and continents. It argues that developers should use strong reads whenever possible and use bounded-staleness reads only where latency demands it. It illustrates write skew with an airline plane-reservation example. It also contrasts Spanner's Paxos-based synchronous out-of-region replication with multi-master replication.
notable: Defines external consistency as stronger than both linearizability and serializability
Explains write skew with an airline free-plane example
Contrasts Spanner's Paxos replication with multi-master replication
Uses TrueTime to serve strong reads without locks or multi-phase consensus
caveats: Promotional content from Google about its own product; claims are not independently verified
Explains the product's approach rather than giving pricing or setup details
